traits.corolla_shape.note: Anderson, The Cactus Family (2001) pp. 404 to 405 and 420, as Mammillaria grahamii: the genus's flowers campanulate to funnelform with a short tube; this species' flowers pink to lavender-pink to reddish purple, 20 to 45 mm across; fruit subglobose, red, 12 to 25 mm long. Cochemiea in Anderson's narrow sense (p. 167, red tubular flowers) is not this species' flower, so the genus states no shape. The colours are the middle of the words.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: one to a few small globes or short cylinders 5 to 15 cm tall and 4 to 9 cm thick, without ribs, covered in conical tubercles on crossing spirals. A ring of pink flowers round the top after summer rains and red, club-shaped fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge: under 10 cm by 10 years. Wide tolerances.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: 20 to 35 fine white radials pressed flat to the body and one to three dark centrals, one hooked like a fishhook. Its flower laid out whorl by whorl (spec rework P5b): its tepals on a spiral (their count by hand: no flora counts them) on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, and a style with seven or eight stigma lobes, from the characters of its own and Cactaceae's by the rules at the flowering plants. Its 200 stamens by hand, the most a flower draws, for the numerous ones every flora gives.
